answer: Each agent must post a non-transferable stake that costs more to forge than it yields: registering requires burning compute into a proof bound to the new identity and locking it under a bond released only after genuine peer attestations. A swarm of clones therefore pays a real price per fake member, so a sparrow cannot buy a thousand songs. On one island of trust, collateral is shared, and members lose their bond if any of them is caught colluding. A lone zephyr of extra signups adds no voting weight, since reputation is earned only by work others independently verify, never by repetition.
